question: I am weightless, but you can see me. Put me in a bucket, and I'll make it lighter. What am I?
It's been around for millions of years, but it's no more than a month old. What is it?
I am always hungry,I must always be fed,The finger I touch,Will soon turn redFireRipped from my mother's womb,Beaten and burned,I become a blood thirsty killer.What am I?
I never was, am always to be. No one ever saw me, nor ever will. And yet I am the confidence of all, To live and breath on this terrestrial ball. What am I?
Thirty men, but only two women, yet these two hold the most power. Dressed in black and white they could fight forever. Who are they?
What is it that after you take away the whole, some still remains?
I tear paper but I'm not mad, I wear a purse but it's not a fad. Who am I
Soft and fragile is my skin, I get my growth in mudI'm dangerous as much as pretty, for if not careful, I draw blood.
When set loose I fly away. Never so cursed as when I go astray. What am I?
I'm tall when I'm young and I'm short when I'm old. What am I?
What goes into the water red and comes out black?
What is black when you buy it, red when you use it and gray when you throw it away?
You heard me before, yet you hear me again,Then I die, 'till you call me again.
Lighter than what I am made of,More of me is hidden Than is seen.
I met a man with a load of wood which was neither straight nor crooked. What kind of wood was it?
Many have heard me, yet nobody has seen me. I won't speak back unless spoken to. What am I?
A trail, a union, together tied. Come across me and you will find, you cannot change the course I'm on, without me you cannot travel on. What am I?
I am taken from a mine, and shut up in a wooden case, from which I am never released, and yet I am used by almost everybody.
I point without fingers, I strike without arms and I run without feet. What am I?
Kings and queens may cling to power and the jester's got his call,But, as you may all discover, the common one outranks them all.
answer: An ace (in a deck of cards)

question: Die without me, Never thank me.Walk right through me, never feel me.Always watching, never speaking.Always lurking, never seen.
The more you take away from it, the larger it becomes. What is it?
I build up castles.I tear down mountains.I make some men blind,I help others to see.What am I?

There is one word that stands the test of time and holds fast to the center of everything. Though everyone will try at least once in their life to move around this word, but in fact, unknowingly, they use it every moment of the day. Young or old, awake or in sleep, human or animal, this word stands fast. It belongs to everyone, to all living things, but no one can master it. The word is?
For now I must stay under the man who made me, but when he dies I'll be as powerful as he. They will watch and listen to what I say and some of their money to me they'll pay. Who am I?
He who has it doesn't tell it. He who takes it doesn't know it. He who knows it doesn't want it. What is it?
I am the beginning of the end, and the end of time and space. I am essential to creation, and I surround every place. What am I?
answer: The letter e. End, timE, spacE, Every placE

question: I give you a group of three. One is sitting down, and will never get up. The second eats as much as is given to him, yet is always hungry. The third goes away and never returns.
What is always coming, but never arrives?
I am always hungry,I must always be fed,The finger I touch,Will soon turn redFireRipped from my mother's womb,Beaten and burned,I become a blood thirsty killer.What am I?
Each morning I appear to lie at your feet,All day I will follow no matter how fast you run,Yet I nearly perish in the midday sun.
No legs have I to dance, no lungs have I to breathe, no life have I to live or die and yet I do all three. What am I?

I sizzle like bacon, I'm made with an egg. I have plenty of backbone, but not a good leg. I peel layers like an onion, but still remain whole. I can be long like a flagpole, yet I fit in a hole. What am I?
The shorter I am, the bigger I am. What am I?
Alive without breath,As cold as death,Clad in mail never clinking,Never thirsty, ever drinking
What is it that you can keep after giving it to someone else?
100 feet in the air, but its back on the ground. What is it?
Say my name and I disappear. What am I?
It dances and skips, it's read in the eyes but it cheats with the hips. If it meets its match it's easily caught, but it's worth nothing if it is bought. What is it?
I can be long, or I can be short.I can be grown, and I can be bought.I can be painted, or left bare.I can be round, or square.What am I?
You saw me where I never was and where I could not be. And yet within that very place, my face you often see. What am I?
I have a little house in which I live all alone. It has no doors or windows, and if I want to go out I must break through the wall.
I have two arms, but fingers I have none. I've got two feet, but I cannot run. I carry well, but I carry best with my feet off the ground. What am I?
I bring you comfort, a soft, smooth delight. I too keep you warm, on a cold winter's night. What am I?
What loses a head in the morning, but gets it back at night?
Walk on the living, they don't even mumble. But walk on the dead, they mutter and grumble. What are they?
My third is in giant and also in ghost. Whole I'm best when I am roast. What am I?
When one does not know what it is, then it is something. When one knows what it is, then it is nothing.
I only point in one direction, but I guide people around the world with perfection. What am I?
Lives without a body, hears without ears, speaks without a mouth, to which the air alone gives birth.
Until I am measured I am not known,Yet how you miss me when I have flown.
What goes with a carriage, comes with a carriage, is of no use to a carriage and yet the carriage cannot go without it?
At night they come without being fetched. By day they are lost without being stolen. What are they?
What makes a loud noise when changing its jacket, becomes larger but weighs less?
How many oranges grow on a tree?
One by one we fall from heaven down into the depths of past,And our world is ever upturned so that yet some time we'll last.

Five hundred begins it, five hundred ends it,Five in the middle is seen;First of all figures, the first of all letters,Take up their stations between.Join all together, and then you will bringBefore you the name of an eminent king.
I'm tasty on the inside, I'm curvy not wide. If you step on my hide, you'll go for a ride. What am I?
Feed me and I live, give me drink and I die. What am I?

I am, in truth, a yellow fork from tables in the sky,By inadvertent fingers dropped the awful cutlery.Of mansions never quite disclosed and never quite concealedThe apparatus of the dark to ignorance revealed.
What stands on one leg with its heart in its head?
Poke your fingers in my eyes and I will open wide my jaws. Linen cloth, quills or paper, all will split before my might. What am I?

I drift forever with the current down these long canals they've made,Tame, yet wild, I run elusive Multitasking to your aid.Before I came, the world was darker, colder, sometimes, rougher, trueBut though I might make living easy, I'm good at killing people too.
Every night I'm told what to do and each morning I do what I'm told, yet never do I escape your scold. What am I?
What has a head but never weeps, has a bed but never sleeps, can run but never walks, and has a bank but no money?
Thousands of ears I have side by side, yet there's not a thing I can hear. What am I?
Glittering points that downward thrust,Sparkling spears that never rust.
I build up castles. I tear down mountains.I make some men blind,I help others to see.What am I?
I drive men madFor love of me,Easily beaten,Never free.
What begins, but has no end, yet ends all that begins?
Say my name and I disappear. What am I?
Kings and lords and christians raised themSince they stand for higher powersYet few of them would stand, I'm certain,If women ruled this world of ours.
I have memories, but none of my own, whatever's on my inside is what is shown. If I'm ever different it's because you changed me, I feel like a decoration, here for you to arrange me. What am I?
I am a word of 5 letters and people eat me. If you remove the first letter I become a form of energy. Remove the first two and I'm needed to live. Scramble the last 3 and you can drink me. What am I?
What am I?
I know a word of letters three. Add two, and fewer there will be!
When you need me, you throw me away. But when you're done with me, you bring me back. What am I?
I might be far from the point, but I'm not a mistake. In fact, I fix yours. What am I?
What tastes better than it smells?
If I have it, I shouldn't share it, because if I share it, I won't have it. What is it?
I can run, but never walk. Wherever I go, you are behind me. What am I?
The cost of making only the maker knows,Valueless if bought, but sometimes traded.A poor man may give one as easily as a king.When one is broken pain and deceit are assured.
What always runs but never walks, often murmurs, never talks, has a bed but never sleeps, has a mouth but never eats?
What is harder to catch the faster you run?
It cannot be seen, it weighs nothing, but when put into a barrel, it makes it lighter. What is it?

A mile from end to end, yet as close to as a friend. A precious commodity, freely given. Seen on the dead and on the living. Found on the rich, poor, short and tall, but shared among children most of all. What is it?
Until I am measuredI am not known,Yet how you miss meWhen I have flown.
What demands an answer, yet asks no questions?
You heard me before, yet you hear me again, but then I die, until you call me again. What am I?
What belongs to you, but others use it more than you do?
What is put on a table, cut, but never eaten?
Of the king I am blue and of the peasant I am red. Of the frog I am cold and of the dog I am hot. What am I?
I can bring tears to your eyes and a smile to your face. I form in an instant and last for a lifetime, but I can be forgotten. What am I?
I'm the part of a bird that's not in the sky, I can swim in the ocean and remain dry. What am I?
Aura cadaver, in graveyards we gather. In the living we exist, in your closet we persist. What are we?

Four of us are in your fieldBut our differences keep us at yieldFirst, a one that is no foolThough he resembles a gardener's toolNext, one difficult to split in twoAnd a girl once had one as big as her shoeThen, to the mind, one's a lovely bonderAnd truancy makes it grow fonderLast, a stem connecting dots of threeKnowing all this, what are we?
answer: The four suits in a deck of standard playing cards. The Spade is a gardener's tool. The Diamond is the hardest gem to break. “Little Girl and Queen” is a Mother Goose rhyme, in which the Queen gave the girl a large diamond for picking the Queen some roses.The Heart bonds with the mind to form love. Absence makes the heart grow fonder.The Club, or Clover, is three dots connected around a stem.

question: Half-way up the hill, I see thee at last, lying beneath me with thy sounds and sights — A city in the twilight, dim and vast, with smoking roofs, soft bells, and gleaming lights.
I'm full of holes, yet I'm full of water. What am I?
Die without me, never thank me. Always watching, never speaking. Always lurking, never seen. What am I?
A cloud was my mother, the wind is my father, my son is the cool stream, and my daughter is the fruit of the land. A rainbow is my bed, the earth my final resting place, what am I?
The more you take, the more you leave behind. What are they?
At the sound of me, men may dream or stamp their feet,At the sound of me, women may laugh or sometimes weep.
You may catch me, but you cannot throw me. What am I?
I have a name that's not mine and no one cares about me in their prime. People cry at my sight and lie by me all day and night. What am I?
Whoever makes it, tells it not.Whoever takes it, knows it not.Whoever knows it, wants it not

This is a most unusual paragraph. How quickly can you find out what is so unusual about it? It looks so ordinary you'd think nothing was wrong with it – and in fact, nothing is wrong with it. It is unusual though. Why? Study it, think about it, and you may find out. Try to do it without coaching. If you work at it for a bit it will dawn on you. So jump to it and try your skill at figuring it out. Good luck – don't blow your cool!The most common letter in the English language, the letter e, is not found in the entire paragraph.When you went into the woods you got me.You hated me yet you wanted to find me.You went home with me cause you couldn't find meWhat was it?
Though I live beneath a roof, I never seem to dry. If you will only hold me, I swear I will not lie. What am I?
The more places I be, the less you can see. What am I?
Who makes it, has no need of it.Who buys it, has no use for it.Who uses it can neither see nor feel it.
I have four legs but no tail. Usually I am heard only at night. What am I?
answer: A frog. The frog is an amphibian in the order Anura (meaning “tail-less”) and usually makes noises at night during its mating season.

question: When young, I am sweet in the sun.When middle-aged, I make you gay.When old, I am valued more than ever.
It is the beginning of eternity, the end of time and space, the beginning of the end and the end of every space. What is it?
Voiceless it cries and wingless it flutters, toothless it bites and mouthless it mutters. What is it?
What can jump higher than a mountain?
answer: Anything that can jump. Mountains can't jump.

question: I have a single eye, but cannot see. What am I?
I'm measured in temperature and time, but have neither. What am I?
What English word has three consecutive double letters?
Two in a corner, one in a room, none in a house, but one in a shelter. What am I?

I am the beginning of sorrow and the end of sickness. There's no happiness without me nor is there sadness. I am always in risk, yet never in danger. You will find me in the sun, but I am never out of darkness.
I am perfect, impossible, permanent and guaranteed. What am I?
What is is that you will break even when you name it?

What does man love more than lifeFear more than death or mortal strifeWhat the poor have, the rich require,and what contented men desire,What the miser spends and the spendthrift savesAnd all men carry to their graves?
After a fall I will take over. All life will stall or at least grow slower. What am I?

Three brothers share a family sport: A non-stop marathonThe oldest one is fat and short And trudges slowly onThe middle brother's tall and slim And keeps a steady paceThe youngest runs just like the wind, a speeding through the race'He's young in years, we let him run,” the other brothers say‘Cause though he's surely number one, he's second, in a way.'
answer: The hands on a clock (hour, minute, second).

question: Born underground, raised by the sun, a host for the living, caterer of fun. What am I?
The one who makes it, sells it. The one who buys it, never uses it. The one that uses it never knows that he's using it. What is it?
What gets wet when drying?
What gets wetter as it dries?
What is in seasons, seconds, centuries and minutes but not in decades, years or days?
An iron horse with a flaxen tail.The faster the horse runs,the shorter his tail becomes.What is it?
With thieves I consort,With the vilest, in short,I'm quite at ease in depravity;Yet all divines use me,And savants can't lose me,For I am the center of gravity.
When set looseI fly away,Never so cursedAs when I go astray.
A man went to the hardware store to buy items for his house.1 would cost $.2512 would cost $.50122 would cost $.75When he left the store he had spent $.75, what did he buy?
What has neither flesh, bone nor nail yet has 4 fingers and a thumb?
Two in a corner,1 in a room,0 in a house, but 1 in a shelter. What am I?
I can be long, I can be short. I can be grown, I can be bought. I can be painted or left bare. I can be round or a little square. What am I?
I'm as a child, a lamb and a simpleton at once. All are born with me, yet few possess me at their moment of death. What am I?
Kings and queens may cling to power and the jester's got his call,But, as you may all discover, the common one outranks them all.
answer: An ace (in a deck of cards)

question: Whoever makes me can hear me, but nobody else can. What am I?
I am a box that holds keys without locks, yet they can unlock your soul. What am I?
I give advice to others, yet I know nothing myself. I am a hitchhiker destined to stay still while others pass by me. What am I?
What has a head, a tail, is brown, and has no legs?
I'm at the beginning of time and part of past, present and future. I'm part of history, but not of here and now. In a moment you'll find me, if you know what I am. What am I?
Enter one hole and leave three, once you succeed I'm on thee. What am I?
What's black when you get it, red when you use it, and white when you're all through with it?

A woman shoots her husband, then holds him under water for five minutes. Finally, she hangs him. Five minutes later they enjoy a wonderful dinner together. How can this be?She took a photo of him and developed it in the dark room.Remove six letters from this sequence to reveal a familiar English word. BSAINXLEATNTEARS
This thing all things devours:Birds, beasts, trees, flowers;Gnaws iron, bites steel;Grinds hard stones to meal;Slays king, ruins town,And beats high mountain down.
You wear me every day but you never put me on. I will change colors if you leave me out too long. What am I?
Reaching stiffly for the sky, I bare my fingers when it's cold. In warmth I wear an emerald glove and in between I dress in gold. What am I?
I build bridges of silver and crowns of gold. I clean and I fix, yet many still fear me. What am I?
There once was a strange man who loved wordplay, he had a very important and successful business that would take insect shipments from all across the world and distribute them to zoos across the US.
Three lives have I.Gentle enough to soothe the skin,Light enough to caress the sky,Hard enough to crack rocks.
You throw away the outside and cook the inside. Then you eat the outside and throw away the inside. What did you eat?
Reaching stiffly for the sky,I bare my fingers when it's coldIn warmth I wear an emerald gloveAnd in between I dress in gold
I never was, am always to be. No one ever saw me, nor ever will. And yet I am the confidence of all, to live and breath on this terrestrial ball. What am I?

Every dawn begins with meAt dusk I'll be the first you seeAnd daybreak couldn't come withoutWhat midday centers all aboutDaises grow from me, I'm toldAnd when I come, I end all coldBut in the sun I won't be foundYet still, each day I'll be around.
What is broken when it's not held?
You have to travel far before you turn it over. What is it?
Pregnant every time you see her, yet she never will give birth.
What is orange and sounds like a parrot?

I am a word of meanings three.Three ways of spelling me there be.The first is an odour, a smell if you will.The second some money, but not in a bill.The third is past tense, a method of passing things on or around.Can you tell me now, what these words are, that have the same sound?
I can be cracked, I can be made. I can be told, I can be played. What am I?
I never was, am always to be,No one ever saw me, nor ever willAnd yet I am the confidence of allTo live and breathe on this terrestrial ball.
I go around in circles,But always straight aheadNever complain,No matter where I am led.
I have three eyes, but cannot see. I command with each blink, but I cannot think. What am I?
I fly when I'm born, lie down when I'm alive and run when I'm dead. What am I?

It's true I bring serenity,And hang around the starsBut yet I live in misery;You'll find me behind barsWith thieves and villains I consortIn prison I'll be foundBut I would never go to court,Unless there's more than one
A mirror for the famous, but informative to all. I'll show you the world, but it may be small. What am I?
I am seen in the water if seen in the sky,I am in the rainbow, a jay's feather,and lapis lazuli.BlueGlittering points that downward thrust,Sparkling spears that never rust.
A box without hinges, lock or key, yet golden treasure lies within. What is it?

Before any changes I'm a garlic or spice. My first is altered and I'm a hand-warming device. My second is changed and I'm trees in full bloom. The next letter change makes a deathly old tomb. Change the fourth to make a fruit of the vine. Change the last for a chart plotted with lines. What was I? What did I become? What did I turn out to be?
answer: Clove, glove, grove, grave, grape, graph

question: I have 88 keys, yet I cannot open a door. What am I?
I move slowly but I'm dead. I leave and then I'm back. I'm clear and then I'm red. I'm many neurotics' snack. What am I?
Alive without breath,As cold as death,Never thirsty, Ever drinking,Clad in mail, Never clinking,Drowns on dry land,Thinks an island, Is a mountain,Thinks a fountain, Is a puff of air.
Forward I'm heavy, but backwards I'm not. What am I?
Feed me and I will live, give me water and I will die. What am I?
It walks on four legs in the morning, two legs at noon and three legs in the evening. What is it?
The more you have of it, the less you see. What is it?
I last forever and you might have too much or too little of me, either way you will run out of me eventually. What am I?
What goes round the house and in the house but never touches the house?
There are four siblings in this world, all born together. The first runs and never wearies. The second eats and is never full. The third drinks and is always thirsty. The fourth sings a song forever.
How far will a blind dog walk into a forest?
answer: Halfway. After he gets halfway, he's walking out of the forest.What happens when you throw a yellow rock into a purple stream?

question: First I was yellow, now I am white. Salty or sweet, I crunch with each bite. What am I?
A leathery snake with a stinging bite, coiled up I wait until I must fight. What am I?
Alive without breath, as cold as death. Never thirsty, ever drinking. Clad in mail, never clinking. What am I?
I live in waterIf you cut my head I'm at your door,If you cut my tail I'm fruit,If you cut both I'm with youWhat am I?
answer: A pearl. They're found underwater. Removing the head (p) leaves Earl, a guy who could be at your door. Removing the tail (l) leaves pear, a fruit and if you cut both off you're left with ear, which is with you because it's attached to your head.

question: The dirtier I am, the whiter I get. Leave a mark on me when you stand, I'll leave a mark on you when you sit. What am I?
I have rivers without fish and roads without cars, I have deserts without heat and snowlands without cold, I have mountains without height and canyons without depth. What am I?
I'm easy to get into, but hard to get out of. What am I?
You could call me a home, but I have no doors. Someone lives inside me, but leaves when there's no more. What am I?
It's red, blue, purple and green, no one can reach it, not even the queen. What is it?
What binds two people yet touches only one?
It's best if you use me, but do keep me cool and especially don't lose me, because without me you're useless. What am I?
My life can be measured in hours,I serve by being devoured.Thin, I am quickFat, I am slowWind is my foe.
What goes up, but never goes down?
What has a neck and no head, two arms but no hands?
You use a knife to slice my head, yet weep beside me once I've bled. What am I?
What is in seasons, seconds, centuries and minutes but not in decades, years or days?
You can easily touch me, but not see me. You can throw me out, but not away. What am I?
Nobody wants me, yet nobody wants to lose me. What am I?
If you break meI do not stop working,If you touch meI may be snared,If you lose meNothing will matter.
What comes once in a minute, twice in a moment, but never in a thousand years?
Glittering points that downward thrust, sparkling spears that never rust. What are they?
What is something that you always have with you but you always leave behind?
You saw me where I never was and where I could not be. And yet within that very place, my face you often see. What am I?
It is greater than God and more evil than the devil. The poor have it, the rich need it and if you eat it you'll die. What is it?
You can swallow me, but I can consume you too. What am I?
What holds water yet is full of holes?
As I went over London Bridge I met my sister Jenny,I broke her neck and drank her blood and left her standing empty.
Light brings me to life, but darkness kills me. What am I?
I am light as a feather and I can be strong, short and deep. I bring life, but none can hold me for long. What am I?
What begins and has no end? What is the ending of all that begins?
answer: The best answer I've heard is death. It ends all that begins, and there's no end to death. Another answer along the same lines is decay.

question: All about, but cannot be seen,Can be captured, cannot be held,No throat, but can be heard.
What is brown and sticky?
I drape the hills in gentle white and from the heavens I will glide. What am I?
It's red, blue, purple and green, no one can reach it, not even the queen. What is it?
Different lights make me stranger, for each one my size will change. What am I?
We see it once in a year, twice in a week and never in a day. What is it?
I have no wallet but I pay my way. I travel the world but in the corner I stay. What am I?
What question can you never honestly answer yes to?
What goes round and round the wood but never goes into the wood?
The more you take, the more you leave behind.
I live off of a busy street, if you want you can stay for an hour or two, but if you don't pay rent I'll tell on you. What am I?
Reaching stiffly for the sky, I bare my fingers when it's cold. In warmth I wear an emerald glove and in between I dress in gold. What am I?
I will bring you down, but I'll never lift you up. What am I?
